name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on the bench, grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders, lower it to mid-chest with elbows about 45 degrees from the body, then press back up.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement, rotator cuff or pectoral injuries. Use a spotter or safety arms for heavy sets.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: On a bench set to 30-45 degrees, lower the bar to the upper chest and press it back up over the shoulders.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement or rotator cuff injuries.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, press them up until the arms are straight, then lower under control.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder or pectoral injuries.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: On a bench inclined to 30-45 degrees, press the dumbbells from upper-chest level to straight arms, then lower slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement.

name: Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Lying on a bench with a slight bend in the elbows, open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch, then bring the dumbbells back together.
contraindications: Avoid deep stretching with shoulder instability or pectoral strain; keep the range comfortable.

name: Push-Up
instructions: From a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders, lower your chest toward the floor keeping the body in a straight line, then push back up.
contraindications: Use caution with wrist or shoulder pain; push-ups on fists or handles can reduce wrist strain.

name: Incline Push-Up
instructions: Place hands on a sturdy raised surface such as a table or bench and perform a push-up; the higher the surface, the easier it is.
contraindications: Use caution with wrist or shoulder pain.

name: Cable Crossover
instructions: Standing between two high pulleys, bring the handles down and together in front of your chest with slightly bent elbows, then return slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder instability.

name: Chest Dip
instructions: Support yourself on the bars, lean the torso forward slightly, lower until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor, then press back up.
contraindications: Avoid with shoulder impingement, anterior shoulder instability, or sternum/AC joint pain.

name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest, press forward until the arms are extended, then return under control.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder injuries.

name: Resistance Band Chest Press
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height, hold the ends at your chest and press forward until the arms are straight, then return slowly.

name: Conventional Deadlift
instructions: With the bar over mid-foot, hinge at the hips and grip it just outside the knees, brace the core with a neutral spine, and stand up by driving through the floor.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with acute lower-back injury, disc herniation, or uncontrolled high blood pressure. Learn technique with light loads.

name: Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Holding the bar at hip height with soft knees, push the hips back and lower the bar along the legs until you feel a hamstring stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back injury or hamstring strain; keep the spine neutral.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Holding dumbbells in front of the thighs, hinge at the hips with soft knees until you feel a hamstring stretch, then return to standing.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back injury or hamstring strain.

name: Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders, pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower to a full hang.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement, elbow tendinopathy, or recent shoulder surgery.

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Hang with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, pull your chin above the bar, then lower slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with elbow or wrist pain.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
instructions: Loop a band over the bar and place a foot or knee in it for assistance, then perform a pull-up. Use a lighter band as you get stronger.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement.

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Seated with thighs secured, pull the bar down to the upper chest while squeezing the shoulder blades down and back, then let it rise under control.
contraindications: Avoid pulling behind the neck; use caution with shoulder impingement.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
instructions: Hinge forward to about 45 degrees with a neutral spine, pull the bar to the lower ribs, then lower it with control.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back injury; a chest-supported row is a safer alternative.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: With one hand and knee on the bench and a flat back, pull the dumbbell toward your hip, then lower it fully.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench and row the dumbbells toward your hips, squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit tall with feet braced, pull the handle to your lower ribs while squeezing the shoulder blades, then extend the arms without rounding the back.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back pain; keep the torso upright.

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Hang under a bar set at waist height with a straight body, pull your chest to the bar, then lower. Bend the knees to make it easier.

name: Resistance Band Row
instructions: Anchor the band in front of you at chest height, pull the handles toward your ribs squeezing the shoulder blades, then return slowly.

name: Superman Hold
instructions: Lie face down and lift the arms, chest and legs slightly off the floor, hold for a few seconds, then lower.
contraindications: Avoid with spondylolisthesis or pain on spinal extension.

name: Face Pull
instructions: With a rope at upper-chest height, pull toward your face while separating the hands and rotating the arms outward, then return slowly.

name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
instructions: Standing with the bar at the collarbone, brace the core and glutes, press the bar straight overhead, then lower it to the start.
contraindications: Avoid with shoulder impingement or limited overhead mobility; use caution with lower-back pain.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Seated with back support and dumbbells at shoulder height, press overhead until the arms are straight, then lower under control.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement.

name: Arnold Press
instructions: Start with dumbbells at chin height and palms facing you, rotate the palms outward as you press overhead, then reverse on the way down.
contraindications: Avoid with shoulder impingement or rotator cuff injury.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height, press upward to full extension, then return slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: With a slight bend in the elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
contraindications: Use light weights and stop below shoulder height if you have impingement.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Standing side-on to a low pulley, raise the handle out to the side to shoulder height, then lower under control.

name: Rear Delt Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back and raise the dumbbells out to the sides, squeezing the shoulder blades, then lower slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back pain; support the chest on an incline bench if needed.

name: Band Pull-Apart
instructions: Hold a band at shoulder height with straight arms and pull it apart until it touches your chest, then return slowly.

name: Pike Push-Up
instructions: From an inverted V position with hips high, bend the elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor, then press back up.
contraindications: Avoid with shoulder impingement, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or glaucoma (head-down position).

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Standing with an underhand grip, curl the bar toward your shoulders keeping the elbows at your sides, then lower fully.
contraindications: Use caution with elbow or wrist pain; an EZ bar may be more comfortable.

name: Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, turning the palms up as you lift, then lower slowly.

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: With palms facing each other, curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, then lower under control.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sitting back on an incline bench with arms hanging, curl the dumbbells up without moving the upper arms, then lower fully.
contraindications: Use caution with anterior shoulder pain due to the stretched position.

name: Cable Curl
instructions: Facing a low pulley, curl the bar or handle toward your shoulders with elbows fixed, then lower slowly.

name: Resistance Band Curl
instructions: Stand on the band and curl the handles toward your shoulders, keeping elbows at your sides.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
instructions: With hands about shoulder-width apart, lower the bar to the lower chest keeping the elbows close to the body, then press up.
contraindications: Use caution with wrist or shoulder pain.

name: Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Facing a high pulley with elbows at your sides, push the bar or rope down until the arms are straight, then return slowly.

name: Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Holding one dumbbell overhead with both hands, lower it behind your head by bending the elbows, then extend back up.
contraindications: Use caution with elbow pain or limited shoulder mobility.

name: Skull Crusher
instructions: Lying on a bench with the bar above your chest, bend the elbows to lower it toward your forehead, then extend the arms.
contraindications: Avoid with elbow tendinopathy; use controlled, moderate loads.

name: Bench Dip
instructions: With hands on the edge of a bench behind you and legs extended, bend the elbows to lower your hips, then press back up.
contraindications: Avoid with shoulder impingement or anterior shoulder pain.

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Perform a push-up with hands close together under the chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
contraindications: Use caution with wrist or elbow pain.

name: Resistance Band Triceps Extension
instructions: Anchor the band high, keep the elbows at your sides and push the band down until the arms are straight.

name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: With the bar on your upper back, brace the core, sit down between your hips until the thighs are at least parallel, then drive back up.
contraindications: Use caution with knee or lower-back injuries; use safety pins or a spotter for heavy sets.

name: Front Squat
instructions: With the bar resting on the front of the shoulders and elbows high, squat down keeping the torso upright, then stand up.
contraindications: Use caution with knee injuries or limited wrist mobility.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest, squat down between your knees with an upright torso, then stand up.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain; limit depth to a pain-free range.

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: With feet shoulder-width apart and arms forward for balance, sit the hips back and down, then stand up.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain; squat to a chair to limit depth if needed.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: With your rear foot on a bench behind you, lower the back knee toward the floor, then drive up through the front foot.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain or poor balance.

name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
instructions: Holding dumbbells at your sides, step forward and lower the back knee toward the floor, then step through into the next lunge.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain or balance problems.

name: Reverse Lunge
instructions: Step one foot back and lower the back knee toward the floor, then push through the front foot to return.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain; usually easier on the knees than forward lunges.

name: Leg Press
instructions: With feet shoulder-width on the platform, lower it until the knees reach about 90 degrees, then press back without locking the knees.
contraindications: Use caution with knee or lower-back injuries; don't let the lower back lift off the seat.

name: Leg Extension
instructions: Seated with the pad on your lower shins, extend the knees to straighten the legs, then lower under control.
contraindications: Use caution with patellofemoral pain or after ACL reconstruction without clinician approval.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
instructions: Holding dumbbells, step one foot onto a bench and drive through it to stand up fully, then step down with control.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain or balance problems.

name: Wall Sit
instructions: With your back against a wall, slide down until the knees are about 90 degrees and hold the position.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain; isometric holds raise blood pressure, so avoid with uncontrolled hypertension.

name: Jump Squat
instructions: Squat down, then jump explosively and land softly with bent knees, going straight into the next rep.
contraindications: Avoid with knee, ankle or back injuries, pregnancy, or pelvic floor issues. Not suitable for beginners without a strength base.

name: Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lying face down with the pad above your heels, curl your heels toward your glutes, then lower slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with a recent hamstring strain.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Kneeling with your ankles anchored, lower your body forward as slowly as possible using the hamstrings, catch yourself with your hands, and push back up.
contraindications: Avoid with a recent hamstring strain or knee pain. Very demanding; start with small ranges.

name: Good Morning
instructions: With a light bar on your upper back and soft knees, hinge forward at the hips with a neutral spine, then return to standing.
contraindications: Avoid with lower-back injury or disc problems; use light loads.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Holding a dumbbell, hinge forward on one leg while the other extends behind you, keeping the hips square, then return to standing.
contraindications: Use caution with balance problems or ankle instability.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: With your upper back against a bench and a padded bar over your hips, drive the hips up until the body is straight from shoulders to knees, then lower.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back pain; don't overextend at the top.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lying on your back with knees bent, squeeze the glutes to lift the hips until the body is straight from shoulders to knees, then lower.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Perform a glute bridge with one leg extended in the air, keeping the hips level.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Hinge at the hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward to swing it to chest height.
contraindications: Avoid with acute lower-back injury; learn the hip hinge first.

name: Cable Pull-Through
instructions: Facing away from a low pulley with the rope between your legs, hinge at the hips, then drive them forward to stand tall.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
instructions: With a mini band around your knees or ankles and a slight squat, step sideways keeping tension on the band.

name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: With a wide stance and toes out, grip the bar inside the knees, keep the chest up and stand by pushing the floor apart.
contraindications: Use caution with hip impingement, groin strain, or lower-back injury.

name: Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Standing on the edge of a step, lower your heels below the step, then rise up onto your toes as high as possible. Hold dumbbells to add load.
contraindications: Use caution with Achilles tendinopathy.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Standing on one foot on a step, lower the heel and then rise onto your toes, using a wall for balance.
contraindications: Use caution with Achilles tendinopathy.

name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Seated with the pad on your thighs, lower the heels, then push up onto your toes.

name: Plank
instructions: Hold a straight line from head to heels on your forearms and toes, bracing the abs and glutes without letting the hips sag.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder pain; hold times raise blood pressure, so breathe steadily.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lying on your side, prop yourself up on one forearm and lift the hips so the body forms a straight line, then hold.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder pain; bend the knees to make it easier.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lying on your back with arms up and knees at 90 degrees, slowly extend the opposite arm and leg while keeping the lower back pressed into the floor.

name: Bird Dog
instructions: On hands and knees, extend the opposite arm and leg until level with your body, hold briefly, then switch sides.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
instructions: Hanging from a bar, raise your knees toward your chest without swinging, then lower slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder or grip problems.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hanging from a bar, raise straight legs to hip height or higher without swinging, then lower under control.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back or shoulder problems.

name: Cable Woodchopper
instructions: Standing side-on to a high pulley, pull the handle diagonally across your body to the opposite hip, rotating through the torso.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back pain or disc problems.

name: Band Pallof Press
instructions: Standing side-on to a band anchored at chest height, press the handle straight out in front of you and resist being pulled sideways, then return.

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sitting with knees bent and torso leaned back, rotate your shoulders from side to side.
contraindications: Avoid with lower-back injury, disc herniation or osteoporosis (loaded spinal flexion and rotation).

name: Crunch
instructions: Lying on your back with knees bent, curl your shoulders off the floor using the abs, then lower slowly. Don't pull on your neck.
contraindications: Avoid with osteoporosis or disc herniation; use caution with neck pain.

name: Mountain Climber
instructions: From a high plank, drive your knees toward your chest one at a time in a running motion, keeping the hips level.
contraindications: Use caution with wrist, shoulder or knee pain.

name: Burpee
instructions: Squat down, place your hands on the floor, jump the feet back to a plank, return the feet, and jump up.
contraindications: Avoid with knee, wrist, shoulder or back injuries, heart conditions without clearance, or pregnancy.

name: Dumbbell Thruster
instructions: Holding dumbbells at shoulder height, squat down, then drive up and use the momentum to press the dumbbells overhead.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder impingement, knee or lower-back pain.

name: Farmer's Carry
instructions: Holding heavy dumbbells at your sides, walk with an upright posture and braced core for distance or time.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back pain or grip injuries.

name: Turkish Get-Up
instructions: Lying down with a kettlebell pressed overhead, stand up step by step while keeping the arm locked and eyes on the bell, then reverse.
contraindications: Use caution with shoulder instability; learn with no weight first.

name: Power Clean
instructions: From the floor, pull the bar explosively by extending the hips and knees, then pull yourself under it and catch it on the front of the shoulders.
contraindications: Advanced technical lift: needs coaching. Avoid with wrist, shoulder or lower-back injuries.

name: Treadmill Running
instructions: Run at a steady or interval pace; use a slight incline (1%) to mimic outdoor running.
contraindications: Use caution with knee, hip or ankle injuries; heart conditions require medical clearance for vigorous cardio.

name: Stationary Cycling
instructions: Adjust the seat so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke and ride at a steady or interval pace.
contraindications: Low impact and usually joint-friendly; heart conditions require medical clearance for vigorous intervals.

name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Drive with the legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs; reverse the order on the return.
contraindications: Use caution with lower-back pain; keep the spine neutral.

name: Brisk Walking
instructions: Walk at a pace where you can talk but not sing, for 20-60 minutes.

name: Jumping Jacks
instructions: Jump the feet wide while raising the arms overhead, then jump back to the start. Step instead of jumping for a low-impact version.
contraindications: Use the step-out version with knee or ankle pain, pelvic floor issues, or pregnancy.

name: High Knees
instructions: Run in place, driving the knees up to hip height and pumping the arms.
contraindications: Use caution with knee or ankle pain.

name: Cat-Cow
instructions: On hands and knees, slowly alternate between arching the back up and letting the belly drop, moving with your breath.

name: Thoracic Spine Rotation
instructions: Lying on your side with knees bent, open the top arm across your body to the other side, rotating through the upper back, then return.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
instructions: From a lunge, place the same-side hand as your front foot on the floor, rotate the other arm to the ceiling, then straighten the front leg to stretch the hamstring.

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Kneeling on one knee, tuck the pelvis under and shift forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip. Hold 30-60 seconds.
contraindications: Pad the knee; use caution with knee pain.

name: Band Shoulder Dislocate
instructions: Holding a band wide with straight arms, slowly bring it over your head and behind you, then back to the front. Widen the grip if needed.
contraindications: Avoid with shoulder instability or a history of dislocation.

name: Deep Squat Hold
instructions: Sink into the bottom of a squat with heels down, using your elbows to gently push the knees out, and hold while breathing slowly.
contraindications: Use caution with knee pain; hold onto a support if balance is an issue.
